newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Australia's Howard links reform to jobs.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Australia's Howard links reform to jobs.

text.p: Australia's Prime Minister John Howard said on Friday that industrial relations reform would increase the nation's productivity and employment levels.
"Industrial relations reform will do good things for productivity and it will also, over time, do very good things for employment," Howard told a business luncheon.

His comments run contrary to Reserve Bank of Australia governor Ian Macfarlane's assertion earlier this week that the passage of the coalition government's industrial relations bill through parliament might have very little effect on employment.
Howard said the government had focussed on the formulation of its industrial relations bill since coming to power in March.
"The industrial relations legislation has been one of the greatest if not the greatest priorities of the coalition government in the economic era since our election," he said.
The Workplace Relations Bill is set to face heated debate later this year in parliament's upper house, the Senate, where the government does not have a clear majority.

The opposition Labor Party, which lost the election and campaigned against the bill, has said it will oppose the legislation while the government has begun talks with the minority Australian Democrats party to win their support.
Howard said the discussions were at a "crucial" stage.
The bill reduces the impact of the union movement and introduces employer-worker negotiations as a centrepiece of the industrial relations system.
Howard noted that future Australian governments were unlikely to have a majority position in the Senate.

"It's going to be very hard to see in the foreseeable future how the government of Australia in the House of Representatives with the present structure of the Senate will have, in its own right, control in the upper house," he said.
